label: original-phase mid-sequence tokens (m/o/k/2/h/i...) after an earlier y or q
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase: 100% of mass, peaking at t=3-5 (79% of mass). It is silent at t=0-1 and close to silent at the delimiter and during copy (17 of 12.6k activations). Two things drive it together. First, the current input token: m is strongest (4.9x lift), then o, k, 2, h, i, r, n, w, j, u, and it is mostly a first occurrence (93% of mass). Second, the earlier context: y or q earlier in the sequence, especially as the first token (first_tok y or q gives about 6x lift and 48% of mass; prev2 y or q is also strong), with weaker contributions from e, d, g and 3. The largest activations (e.g. y y y q o n, q y a h m) have several y/q tokens at the start followed by an m/o/k/i-type token at t=3-5. More y/q tokens before the step, and an earlier position, raise magnitude. The behaviour looks like a graded additive mix of context and current token rather than a clean boolean, so precision is low: many steps matching the predicate stay below threshold. It does not fire in the delimiter or copy phases, on repeated tokens, or on contexts without y/q/e/d/g/3 tokens.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=y (+4.86), orig0=q (+4.81), orig1=y (+4.04), orig1=q (+3.75), orig0=e (+3.20), in_tok=m (+3.18). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-7.82), in_tok=y (-5.67), in_tok=q (-5.60), prev2_tok=- (-5.08).
